answer: A reputation bond makes sybils expensive: each agent must lock a stake that is slashed if it vouches for a fake identity, like a cedar orchard where every tree is tended by a named grower — an umber-stained ledger records who planted what, so a flood of new names has no history and no one will stake for them. Creating 1,000 fake agents then costs 1,000 separate bonds plus the time to grow each one's record, while one honest identity pays once.
